data.title: Canada offers concessions in a bid to avoid Trump’s 50% tariffs: NYT
data.description:
Canada has offered a set of trade proposals as it negotiates with the U.S. to avoid 50% tariffs that the Trump administration plans to impose on the country’s exports in less than two weeks, The New York Times reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The Canadian package includes a move to eliminate a retaliatory tariff on U.S.-made autos introduced in response to a similar U.S. measure, said two people with knowledge of Canada’s stance in the negotiations.

The government of Prime Minister Mark Carney expects to significantly lower current trade levies and has emphasized that it will seek a more comprehensive deal, not a piecemeal agreement with the U.S.

“We’re not interested in a very targeted deal,” Carney told reporters on Thursday, adding, “We’re interested in a more comprehensive deal, more global deal.”

The concessions represent a major reaction from Ottawa to President Donald Trump’s recent proclamations to impose a 50% tariff on a range of Canadian imports, effective August 19, in response to what he claimed was Canada’s discriminatory treatment of American products.

$20B Canadian exports ranging from wine and hockey sticks to paper and furniture were targeted in Trump’s orders, renewing a trade dispute with the country’s northern neighbor, its second-largest trading partner after Mexico.

One of the people said that Canada is not ready to sign any trade deal that doesn’t take into account tariffs on the automotive industry, a leading employer in the country’s most populous state, Ontario.

Among Canadian proposals are plans to ensure the country’s critical mineral exports to the U.S. and measures to cooperate on energy and defense, which may include Canada joining Trump’s proposed “Golden Dome” missile defense shield.

However, despite media reports to the contrary, the Canadian negotiators have not agreed to return American wine and spirits to government-owned provincial liquor shops but told the U.S. mediators that the boycott will end once Carney’s government presents a satisfactory trade deal to those provinces.

Canada is looking to reach a “political agreement” rather than a formal trade pact with the U.S., one of the people said. Not only would such a deal not require Congressional backing, but it would also be easier to revise under a future government, he added.

data.title: Trending stocks this week as SpaceX, Palantir earnings and jobs data drive markets
data.description:
Wall Street ended the week higher, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) and the S&P 500 (SP500) closing at record highs as investors weighed a deluge of corporate earnings, including results from SpaceX (SPCX) and Palantir Technologies (PLTR), alongside weaker-than-expected U.S. payrolls data.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July, missing economists' expectations for an 88,000 increase and reversing June's revised gain of 20,000, according to data released Friday by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

For the week, the S&P (SP500) added +3.6%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) climbed +5.2%, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) advanced +3.0%.

Here's what caught investor attention this week:

SpaceX's (SPCX) first earnings report as a public company showed strong revenue growth. However, the stock dropped 14% in the wake of the report, as investors were unsettled by the company's plans to sharply increase spending on AI infrastructure. Capital expenditures climbed to $18.4B during the second quarter, up from $10.1B in the first quarter and more than six times the $2.8B spent a year earlier. Nearly $15.8B of that total was invested in the company's AI business.

AMD (AMD) shares fell 7% on Wednesday as investors likely expected a larger increase in its guidance for the coming quarter. The company did beat expectations on its headline numbers, with revenue soaring 50% to $11.54B. Looking ahead, AMD said it expects third-quarter revenue to be between $12.7B and $13.3B, with the mid-point of $13B well above the $12.51B consensus. Adjusted gross margin is expected to be 56%, AMD added.

Amazon's (AMZN) market capitalization surpassed $3T for the first time in its history. This came after a strong post-earnings rally fueled by better-than-expected results and optimism about the growth of its AWS cloud business and AI investments.

Palantir (PLTR) posted results well above Wall Street expectations, driven by continued strength in its AI business. The company also increased its full-year outlook. Investors responded enthusiastically, sending the stock up roughly 37% in the week.

President Donald Trump criticized ExxonMobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX), saying they were "making too much money" as gasoline prices surged. He urged the oil giants to share more of their profits with consumers by lowering fuel prices.

AstraZeneca (AZN) and Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) were in the spotlight after The Financial Times reported the two held preliminary talks about a potential merger that would have created one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, with a combined value approaching $400B . The talks were at an early stage, and no deal has yet been reached.

Sandisk (SNDK) shares fell after the storage maker issued mixed guidance that overshadowed stronger-than-expected results for the fiscal fourth quarter. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Sandisk expects adjusted earnings to be between $44 and $46 per share, with the midpoint above the $44.72 per share estimate. Revenue is forecast to be between $10.3B and $10.8B, with the midpoint of $10.55B below the $10.82B estimate.

Novo Nordisk (NVO) slipped despite raising its full-year outlook for the second time this year, citing increased expectations for GLP-1 product sales. The Danish drugmaker now expects sales and operating profit to decline by no more than 6% at constant exchange rates this year, improving from its previous forecast of declines of up to 12%.

The Trade Desk (TTD) shares tumbled after the bell as investors reacted to second-quarter earnings miss and signs of slowing momentum at the digital advertising platform. Revenue rose 3% year-over-year to $715M, below consensus estimates of $751.4M. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.34, missing expectations of $0.40. Chief Executive Officer Jeff Green said the results “did not meet the standard we set for ourselves,” citing a complex environment for marketers.

Tesla (TSLA) confirmed on Thursday that its massive Terafab will be built in Grimes County, Texas. The Austin-based company broke ground on its research fab on the North Campus of Giga Texas in April, a site that it calls a precursor to Terafab. The initial investment is $16.8B.

Western Digital (WDC) shares fell even as the storage maker reported fourth-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast. The firm earned an adjusted $3.56 per share as revenue rose 44% year-over-year to $3.75B. Analysts had expected the company to earn $3.31 per share on $3.7B in revenue.

Caterpillar (CAT) surged after reporting record second quarter results, helped by booming demand for power generation equipment, construction machinery and mining products. The heavy equipment maker reported sales of $20.54B, ahead of the Wall Street consensus estimate of $19.2B. Adjusted earnings came in at $8.17 a share, well above analysts' expectations of $6.20.

data.title: Real estate stocks edge down as investor attention turns to cyclicals
data.description:
Real estate stocks suffered as investor attention once again shifted to technology and other cyclical stocks.

Wall Street finished the week higher, with the benchmark S&P 500 hitting fresh all-time highs as investors digested key earnings from technology giants alongside the latest payrolls data.

A sharp contraction in the U.S. labor market sent Treasury bond yields tumbling, sparking investor optimism that the Federal Reserve will hold off on imminent interest rate hikes.

The benchmark U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) declined ten basis points to 4.65% during the course of the week.

However, mortgage rates continued to hover over year-ago levels, dragging purchase and refinance demand lower. Higher mortgage rates have weakened overall housing demand.

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) decreased 0.12% week-over-week to 286.26 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was down 0.20% to $44.98.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index pulled back 0.61%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index declined 0.62%.

Weekly Winners & Losers

This week, CoStar (CSGP) topped the largecap gainers, advancing 5.15% to $30.24.

The real estate services provider had reported mixed Q2 results and guidance in the prior week and was downgraded at William Blair. However, analyst Stephen Sheldon was optimistic about the company's medium-term outlook.

American Homes 4 Rent (AMH) (+3.62% W/W to $34.63) was the second-biggest winner, extending gains from the previous week when the residential REIT reported second-quarter earnings above analyst expectations.

Host Hotels & Resorts (HST) stood out as the top loser, pulling back 7.32% to $23.29.

The hotel REIT reported a Q2 beat, but analysts sentiment was slightly negative to neutral, centering on flow-through sensitivity, cost inflation, and demand cadence.

Federal Realty Investment Trust (FRT) (-4.35% W/W to $118.69) followed, having priced a $400M exchangeable senior notes offering due 2031 this week.

Among midcap stocks, Ryman Hospitality Properties (RHP) led the weekly losers, retreating 9.58% from the previous week to $120.84. The hotel REIT reported mixed Q2 earnings results, but analysts sentiment were said to be neutral to slightly skeptical, focusing on brand fee pressure, OEG timing/proceeds, and uncertainty items.

Acadia Realty Trust (AKR) (-8.10% W/W to $20.65) and Opendoor Technologies (OPEN) (-7.56% W/W to $3.49) followed, with Q2 earnings that failed to impress.

Compass (COMP) led the winners, adding 10.45% week-over-week to $12.58, even as Q2 earnings missed estimates. The stock was gaining on the back of a positive Q3 guidance.

Among smallcap stocks, Real Brokerage (REAX) (+33.75% W/W to $2.14) gained the most amid Q2 revenue exceeding expectations. RE/MAX Holdings (RMAX) added 22.50% to $11.37 even as Q2 earnings fell short of expectations.

JBG SMITH Properties (JBGS) (-13.45% W/W to $12.16) led the weekly decliners.

Community Healthcare Trust (CHCT) was also a notable loser, declining 13.44% to $15.85. The healthcare REIT posted a Q2 miss and reduced its quarterly dividend by ~31%.

data.title: Iran says Hormuz deal close amid attack on UAE tanker
data.description:
Iran said on Saturday that talks with Oman over reopening the Strait of Hormuz were in the final stages, while the UAE accused the country of attacking one of its tankers while it was transiting the key maritime route.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that talks to reopen the strait were “approaching the final stages” but cautioned that fully reopening the vital shipping lane will depend on how the U.S. commits to a June memorandum of understanding.

“The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is subject to other conditions and compensation for the violation of the memorandum of understanding by the United States,” Araghchi said, referring to the U.S.-Iran peace deal that fell apart last month.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a core flashpoint in the conflict, with a U.S. official telling Reuters on Friday that Washington will lift its blockade of Iranian ports once Tehran reaches a deal to restore commercial ​shipping through the waterway.

The United Arab Emirates, meanwhile, accused Iran of attacking a tanker belonging to the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz early on Saturday.

No injuries have been reported, and the situation has been brought under control, according to the state-run WAM news agency.

The UAE foreign ministry described the incident as a “hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties.”

data.title: Earnings Scorecard: 95% of healthcare firms deliver EPS wins this week
data.description:
Major healthcare heavyweights, including Pfizer (PFE), Merck (MRK), and Eli Lilly (LLY), reported their quarterly earnings this week, pushing the healthcare sector into positive territory after five consecutive sessions of losses.

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) rose 1.36% in the week so far. On a YTD basis, XLV has added more than 5%; however, it is lagging behind the broader S&P 500 index (SP500), which advanced 12.63%.

Earnings Roundup

Overall, 22 healthcare firms reported their earnings in the week ended August 7. Of these, one missed earnings estimates while the remaining 21 posted better-than-expected EPS.

In terms of revenue, two firms lagged analysts’ consensus, and 20 posted top lines above expectations.

Below is a snapshot of the quarterly print of some major firms in the healthcare sector:

Pfizer’s (PFE) second quarter results topped Wall Street expectations. The company raised its full-year revenue outlook, driven by stronger-than-expected performance from its non-COVID portfolio. It reported adjusted EPS of $0.77, while revenue rose 2.6% year over year to $15.03B. The drugmaker raised its 2026 revenue guidance by $500M at the midpoint to a range of $60.5B-$62.5B and reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance of $2.80-$3.00.

Merck (MRK) also reported a better-than-expected Q2 print driven by continued strength in its blockbuster cancer drug Keytruda, as well as strong uptake for newer drugs like Winrevair. The drugmaker posted an adjusted loss of $0.13 per share while revenue rose 5.1% year over year to $16.61B, led by Keytruda, which generated $8.4B in sales.

Eli Lilly’s (LLY) weight loss portfolio continued to power its financials as shares jumped nearly 5% in post-earnings price action. Lilly posted $23B in revenue while adjusted EPS increased ~33% YoY to $8.38, driven by its injectable GLP-1 drugs and its newly launched weight-loss pill, Foundayo. LY's injectable weight-loss therapy Zepbound and its diabetes counterpart Mounjaro added $4.9B and $9.9B to the topline, respectively. Foundayo brought in sales worth $98M.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) was the only firm that missed earnings estimates, while Zoetis (ZTS) and  STERIS (STE) reported revenue below analysts’ consensus.

Out of the pharma companies that reported earnings this week, three were biotechnology firms, and five were pharmaceutical companies. Eleven of those belonged to the health care equipment industry, while three came from Life Sciences Tools & Services.

Upcoming Earnings

With the earnings season drawing to a close, only one major healthcare firm, Cardinal Health (CAH), is due to report its results next week.

data.title: Insider trades: Microsoft, Meta, Pfizer among notable names
data.description:

  • Microsoft (MSFT) saw two executives divest a small part of their positions in the company this week. EVP and Chief Marketing Officer Takeshi Numoto sold 4,810 shares at $496.48 each for ~$2.39M. The transaction represented about 10.13% of his direct holdings, leaving him with 42,677 shares. Meanwhile, Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial, sold 10,000 shares at $487.89 each for around $4.88M. The sale accounted for about 9.05% of his direct holdings, reducing his stake to 100,447 shares.

  • CrowdStrike (CRWD) Chief Financial Officer Burt Podbere sold 7,622 shares at $194.34 to $196.62 each for around $1.48M. The transaction represented about 1.08% of his direct holdings, leaving him with 696,818 shares.
  • Delta Air Lines (DAL) also saw several executives slash their positions in the company. The biggest sale, however, came from CEO Edward Bastian, who diluted 13.15% of his direct holdings. Bastian sold 206,510 shares at $92.80 each for a total of $19.16M, reducing his stake to 1,363,448 shares.
  • Pfizer (PFE) Senior Vice President and Controller Jennifer D'Amico divested 10.28% of her direct holding in the firm. She sold 3,278 shares at $25.40 each for ~$83,261. The sale left her with 28,611 shares.

Director Ronald Blaylock purchased 39,231 shares at $25.46 each for $998,821, increasing his holdings to 71,688 shares.   • Tilray Brands (TLRY) Chief Financial Officer Carl Merton purchased 10,000 shares at $4.62 each for $46,200, bringing his total holdings to 139,753 shares.

data.title: Nvidia eyeing up to $3B investment in Blackstone-backed power firm: The Information
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) plans to invest up to $3B in Lancium, an energy infrastructure company backed by private equity firm Blackstone (BX), The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The semiconductor firm will initially invest $2B in Lancium in exchange for a roughly 20% stake before adding another $1B depending on whether the company reaches certain targets, including grid hookups.

The deal values Lancium and its land and power connections at approximately $10B in enterprise value. The funding is expected to support Lancium’s plans to broaden its operations as it’s preparing for a potential initial public offering next year.

The company owns the 1.2 GW ⁠Lancium ​Clean Campus in Abilene, Texas, which serves as the inaugural site of the Stargate project, an artificial intelligence-focused infrastructure initiative unveiled by President Donald Trump in January 2025.

Led by OpenAI (OPENAI) and the global tech investor SoftBank (SFTBY) (SFTBF) (SOBKY), Stargate aims to invest $500B over four years to build new AI infrastructure for the ChatGPT maker.

Nvidia (NVDA) and Lancium did not immediately return requests for comment.

data.title: Consumer Staples Earnings Scorecard: Profit holds up despite mixed revenue
data.description:
Ten S&P 500 consumer staples (XLP) companies reported quarterly results this week, with eight beating Wall Street's earnings estimates despite a mixed showing on revenue.

Earnings highlights

  • Beat on both EPS and revenue estimates: Kraft Heinz (KHC), Kimberly-Clark (KMB), Clorox (CLX), Sysco (SYY), Monster Beverage (MNST), Molson Coors (TAP), and Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP).
  • Beat EPS but missed revenue estimate: Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM).
  • Met EPS but missed revenue estimate: Tyson Foods (TSN).
  • Missed both EPS and revenue estimates: Kenvue (KVUE).
  • On a year-over-year basis, seven of the 10 companies increased earnings per share, while six posted higher revenue. Kimberly-Clark, Archer-Daniels-Midland, Sysco, Monster Beverage, Kenvue, and Keurig Dr Pepper delivered increases in both earnings and revenue, while Tyson Foods grew EPS despite a decline in revenue.

Archer-Daniels-Midland posted the largest EPS beat (+$0.40/share) but also the biggest revenue miss (-$379.6M versus estimates).

Sysco delivered the largest revenue beat (+$233.2M), while Kimberly-Clark recorded the biggest EPS beat among household products companies (+$0.11/share).

Notable earnings

The Kraft Heinz Company (KHC) reported a 1.4% decrease in revenue during Q1 to $6.05B. Organic sales fell 1.3% during the quarter to miss the consensus expectation. Looking ahead, the firm sees FY26 organic sales down 0.5% to down 2.0% and EPS of $2.03 to $2.09 (midpoint $2.06) vs. $2.03 consensus and the prior expectation of $1.98 to $2.10.

Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) easily beating Q2 adjusted earnings expectations and raising its full-year profit outlook for a second time, driven by a favorable margin backdrop across biofuels and momentum in nutrition. Q2 profit jumped to $908M, or $1.87/share, from $219M, or $0.45/share, in the year-earlier quarter, and revenue rose 7.2% Y/Y to $22.68B.

Kimberly-Clark (KMB) reported net sales of $4.19B, up 0.6% year over year, but below the $4.22B consensus estimate. Organic sales were broadly flat as favorable currency was offset by the exit of its U.S. private-label diaper business and a social media-related disruption in China that reduced growth by roughly 50 basis points. Adjusted EPS attributable to the company rose 10.4% year over year to $2.12.

Kenvue (KVUE) missed Wall Street's estimates on both earnings and revenue, reporting adjusted EPS of $0.31, one cent below consensus, while revenue rose 3.1% year over year to $3.96B but fell $10M short of expectations.

data.title: Earnings scorecard: 9 out of 10 Communication Services companies deliver EPS wins this week
data.description:
Communication Services (XLC) stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from companies including The Walt Disney (DIS), The Trade Desk (TTD), and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), among others.

In this week's earnings recap, 10 tickers reported results, of which nine companies exceeded EPS expectations, while The Trade Desk (TTD) missed expectations. On the revenue front, six companies beat revenue consensus estimates, while four communication services companies failed to meet Street expectations.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some of the key players who reported results this week:

The Walt Disney Company (DIS) reported third-quarter earnings that topped expectations, supported by strong performance at its U.S. theme parks and a major box office hit from Toy Story 5.

Adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.06, ahead of the $1.86 analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg, while revenue rose 7% to $25.25B, slightly below expectations of $25.39B.

The Experiences segment was a key driver, with operating income rising 20% to $3.02 billion on revenue of $9.97B. Entertainment remained Disney’s (DIS) largest segment, with revenue of $11.35B, though it fell short of expectations. Sports revenue of $4.5B also missed estimates.

Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) reported better-than-feared second quarter profit, which was offset by a miss in revenue and in-line adjusted EBITDA.

In the second quarter, significant legal expenses related to its pending merger with Paramount Skydance (PSKY) weighed on profitability, while the company's streaming segment outperformed with a 10% increase in revenue and an 11% increase in streaming distribution revenue.

The Warner Bros. studio segment, however, suffered a 39% drop in revenue as theatrical release sales were pressured by the disappointing box office for this quarter’s slate of movies. Additionally, TV revenue was down 45% due to lower intercompany content licensing resulting from the timing of renewals.

The Trade Desk (TTD) shares tumbled around 22.5% after the bell as investors reacted to the company’s second-quarter earnings miss and signs of slowing momentum at the digital advertising platform.

Revenue rose 3% year-over-year to $715M, below consensus estimates of $751.4M. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.34, missing expectations of $0.40.

Profitability also declined, with net income falling to $64M from $90M a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $241M from $271M, with margin contracting to 34% from 39%.

Looking ahead, TTD forecasts third-quarter revenue of at least $650M compared to a consensus of $650.19M and adjusted EBITDA of about $160M.

Overall, the Communication Services sector (XLC) has slipped more than 5.5% so far this year, underperforming the broader S&P 500 Index, which is up about 12.6%.

data.title: Todd Blanche confirmed as next U.S. attorney general
data.description:
The Senate Republicans narrowly confirmed Todd Blanche as the next U.S. attorney general early Saturday morning, putting President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer in charge of the Department of Justice.

The Republican-led Senate voted 50-49 to make Blanche the second confirmed attorney general since Trump returned to the White House last year with a stated desire to use the law enforcement agency to investigate his political enemies. While Blanche has already been leading the department in an acting capacity, his confirmation could free him to pursue the Trump administration’s agenda even more aggressively.

Blanche said on social media that he was “deeply honored by the trust and confidence President Trump has placed in me,” adding that he was “grateful” to senators for working late to confirm him.

The vote followed a tumultuous confirmation fight that exposed deep concerns — from some Republicans as well as Democrats — about installing Trump’s close ally atop a Justice Department that historically prided itself on its independence from the White House.

In the end, Blanche was confirmed by the narrowest of margins, opposed by two Republicans — Sens. Susan Collins of Maine and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska — and by every Democrat.

The path to confirmation for Blanche was unusually rocky, due in large part to Republican concerns about a controversial settlement of Trump’s lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service.

Under pressure, Blanche publicly promised in writing that the department would abandon Trump’s proposed $1.8 billion compensation fund for the president’s allies, including those who attacked the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, and rein in another piece of the settlement designed to shield Trump and his family from IRS tax audits.

His appeals were enough to win over Republican Sen. Bill Cassidy, the decisive vote who threw his support behind Blanche Friday morning. Cassidy said no other nominee may be able to run the department better under Trump and suggested Blanche’s role as Trump’s former criminal defense lawyer can make him more effective at pushing back on the president’s demands.

“This is not a referendum on President Trump. It is a decision regarding Mr. Blanche in very specific circumstances,” said Cassidy, who lost his primary this year to a Trump-backed challenger.

Sen. Dick Durbin of Illinois, the top Democrat on the Senate Judiciary Committee, said confirming Blanche would be a “serious mistake.” He begged his colleagues not to be on the “wrong side” of history.

“If there is ever a moment in history when we need an Attorney General above reproach, who is clearly dedicated to ending corruption, even at the highest level of our government, it’s right now,” Durbin said.

Blanche’s loyalty to Trump left senators skeptical

The vote capped off a bruising confirmation fight, with Blanche’s loyalty to Trump at the center of the stalemate.

Blanche was elevated to the top Justice Department post in an acting capacity after Trump fired Pam Bondi in April. Blanche moved swiftly to advance the president’s interests, accelerating investigations into Trump’s perceived foes and announcing the settlement that created the $1.8 billion “Anti-Weaponization Fund” to compensate people who feel mistreated by the criminal justice system and provided Trump and family members with immunity from tax audits.

The controversial settlement threatened to torpedo Blanche’s nomination until he formally rescinded the fund in writing under pressure from Republican Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina. The deal reached between the senators and the department unlocked a vote in the Senate Judiciary Committee, which advanced Blanche’s nomination earlier this week

Even after the deal, Blanche faced opposition from some Republican senators concerned with the “Anti-Weaponization Fund” and the tax audit immunity deal.

Murkowski announced early Friday that she would join Collins in opposing Blanche’s nomination, saying the country needs an attorney general “who will check the worst impulses of this administration.”

Former prosecutor rises as Trump’s defender

A former federal prosecutor in New York, Blanche rose to public prominence as a lead attorney on Trump’s defense team, including during the Republican’s hush money trial in New York. He also defended Trump against criminal charges in the two federal cases brought by the Biden administration’s Department of Justice — an experience Blanche has said provided him a firsthand look at what he contends was the weaponization of the criminal justice system against Trump.

Blanche entered the Justice Department last year as deputy attorney general under Bondi, overseeing the agency’s day-to-day operations and serving as the public face for high-profile and controversial matters, like the release of millions of investigative files related to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.

Democrats have accused Blanche of prioritizing his loyalty to Trump above all else through investigations against Trump foes such as former FBI Director James Comey and a radical reshaping of the department. Under Bondi and Blanche’s leadership, the department has lost thousands of employees through firings, resignations or voluntary departures.

Blanche’s supporters say his experience as a federal prosecutor and the trust he earned from Trump in the courtroom make him better equipped than Bondi to explain to the White House the legal constraints of its demands. Republicans have also touted his efforts to bring down violent crime, tackle illegal immigration and combat violent cartels and drug trafficking.

Sen. Chuck Grassley, the Republican chairman of the Judiciary Committee, gave a full-throated endorsement of Blanche ahead of voting, saying he’s led the Justice Department with distinction. “Mr. Blanche is the right choice,” he said.

But it remains unclear whether Blanche will fare any better in delivering on Trump’s desire for retribution than Bondi, whom Trump fired amid resistance from judges, grand jurors and the department’s own workforce as prosecutors sought to establish criminal conduct by one Trump foe after another.

Shortly after Blanche took the top post, the Justice Department moved to indict Comey on charges of threatening the 47th president by posting a social media photograph of seashells in the numerical arrangement of “86 47.” Comey’s lawyers are pressing to have the case dismissed, accusing the department of misleading judges, submitting documents containing false statements and withholding key facts.

Blanche has also appointed Joseph diGenova, a former Justice Department prosecutor from the Reagan administration, to oversee a Florida-based investigation into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired over the last decade to undermine Trump. But it remains uncertain whether that probe will result in any criminal charges.
